query: Which reproducible simulation frameworks and parameter choices best model within-team autocorrelation, ICCs, and realistic missing-data mechanisms for power and sample-size estimates in longitudinal DevOps trials?

response.query: Which reproducible simulation frameworks and parameter choices best model within-team autocorrelation, ICCs, and realistic missing-data mechanisms for power and sample-size estimates in longitudinal DevOps trials?
response.answer: For longitudinal DevOps trials, use mixed-effects models and multiple imputation for missing data, with Monte Carlo simulations for power and sample size estimates. Focus on intra-cluster correlation (ICC) and realistic missing-data mechanisms.

results.title: Applications of Simulation for Missing Data Issues in Longitudinal Clinical Trials | Springer Nature Link
results.content: Although a lot of research has been devoted to statistical methods for missing data, there is no universally best approach for analysis. To evaluate and implement statistical analysis models for missing data, Monte-Carlo simulations are often used. In this chapter, we present a few simulation-based approaches related to missing data issues in longitudinal clinical trials. First, a simulation-based approach is developed for generating monotone missing data under a variety of missing data mechanism, which allows users to specify the expected proportion of missing data at each longitudinal time point. Specifically, we apply a delta-adjustment approach to account for the potential difference in the estimated treatment effects between the mixed model (typically used as the primary model in clinical trials) and the multiple imputation model used to facilitate the tipping point analysis. ### Bayesian Sensitivity Analysis in Survival and Longitudinal Trials with Missing Data. On analysis of longitudinal clinical trials with missing data using reference-based imputation.

results.title: Simulation for power in designing cluster randomized trials -
results.content: As a biostatistician, I like to be involved in the design of a study as early as possible. I always like to say that I hope one of the first conversations an investigator has is with me, so that I can help clarify the research questions before getting into the design questions related to measurement, unit of randomization, and sample size. To estimate power under a range of scenarios, I’ve written two functions to define the data generation process, one to generate the data, and a final one to generate a single data set and estimate the parameters of a mixed effects model. The variance of the cluster-level random effect is based on a conversion of the intra-cluster correlation (*ICC*) to the logistic scale, which is done through a call to the function `iccRE`. Here is an example setting the *ICC* at 0.025, the control proportion at 40%, and an effect size that translates to a 30% reduction (so that the treatment proportion will be 28%).
